rv.q: Lombe's touching, emotionally intelligent and contemporary black British love story is itself easy to fall in love with.
Lombe makes her mark as one of its most exciting and distinctive voices.
This, you see, is the skill of Lombe and the entire Shifters team: to wear tender profundity deceptively lightly.
Shifters is a brilliant addition to this canon, and to a theatreland that’s finding new audiences to love it, argue with it, and bring it to life.
For all its structural cleverness — with its echoes of Nick Payne’s hit play Constellations — it’s the warmth and subtlety of Lombe’s emotional insights that give the script its megawatt appeal.

Shifters is a bittersweet but heartening love story whose transition to the theatrical mainstream is accompanied by much glitzy fanfare courtesy of its starry new producing line-up: actor Idris Elba, TV presenter Maya Jama and rapper Little Simz.
Lombe’s writing, suffused with wit and warmth, is exquisitely poetic at times.

cn.t: Critics widely praise Shifters as a lyrical, bittersweet romcom, with standout performances and Benedict Lombe's witty, poetic script earning near-universal acclaim in its West End transfer.
